x: should i balance the grinding wheel? it's a breeze with our »»toolbalancer«« balancing system our balancing system extends tool life precision-balanced tools are extremely important for modern cutting machines. unbalances in grinding wheels, tooling systems, and rotors cause wear and tear or even damage—regular balancing prevents downtime and reduces your costs. top efficient balancing with the zoller »toolbalancer« long balancing times lead to downtime and a loss of quality. our »toolbalancer« not only allows for high-precision balancing of tool holders, grinding wheels, and rotors—its automated measurement sequence also significantly speeds up the procedure. it can accommodate your current requirements as well as future developments you can’t yet anticipate: thanks to its modular design, the »toolbalancer« can be adjusted to your specific needs. the device can be used intuitively and effortlessly via touchscreen, keyboard, or mouse—whichever best suits your workflow. this allows you to focus on working and producing effectively and to a high standard. as a result, you’ll measurably reduce your scrap rates, machine downtime, and production costs! learn more about »toolbalancer« center higher cutting performance longer tool life better component quality what is wheel balancing? balancing reduces or, ideally, corrects any unbalances present in any rigid body rotating about a fixed axis. these unbalances result from uneven mass distribution within the grinding wheel; the reference point in each case is the axis of rotation of the grinding spindle. the primary goal of balancing is to perform correction of all centrifugal forces acting on the rotating spindle so that the spindle bearing is not subjected to any additional forces. top how do unbalances develop in grinding wheels? unbalances in a grinding wheel can occur as early as during the manufacturing process; for example: slight deviations from the ideal geometric shape or a perfectly symmetrical shape due to production errors, other manufacturing defects, or uneven density of the grinding wheel’s structure (result: unbalanced weight distribution). above all, however, unbalances are caused by wear and tear during the grinding process. examples of this include: uneven abrasion during the grinding process, pollution from chips or coolants and lubricants, and stress and deformation caused by clamping forces, cutting forces, and centrifugal forces. additional problems can arise from improper storage or incorre

d: Balancing Tools Made Easy Unbalances in your tool quickly become a problem in several ways: They cause the tool to run out of round, put strain on the spindle and the machine, impa
x: balancing tools made easy unbalances in your tool quickly become a problem in several ways: they cause the tool to run out of round, put strain on the spindle and the machine, impair machining performance, and ultimately compromise the overall process reliability. top what are the consequences of unbalance in the tool? tools that run unevenly cannot be used consistently with the precision you need for your work. the resulting vibrations not only reduce overall machining performance, but also cause defects on the workpieces—such as chatter marks—which may require rework. unbalances in the tool thus lead to very tangible quality losses and are a hazard to the process reliability of your operations. furthermore, these unbalances also reduce the lifetime of the spindle and possibly the machine—the costs associated with this quickly exceed the expenses incurred by balancing the tools more frequently. top what does "unbalance" mean? the term “unbalance” describes the ubiquitous phenomenon in rotating bodies whereby their mass is not distributed symmetrically about the body’s axis of rotation. there are essentially three types of unbalance: static unbalance: here, the center of gravity of the rotating body lies outside the axis of rotation. this can already be measured when the body is at rest. original unbalance: the center of gravity lies on the axis of rotation; the unbalance becomes measurable only when the object is in rotational motion. dynamic unbalance: the term “dynamic unbalance” encompasses the other two forms of unbalance, in any combination of static unbalance and original unbalance. this is the norm for technical rotors. each specific form of unbalance can be corrected by adjusting the rotating body in an appropriate manner. during rotation, an unbalance becomes more noticeable the greater the unbalance is (linear increase) and the faster the rotational movement is (quadratic increase). the faster the rotational movement, the more important balancing becomes, and the more important it is to reduce the residual unbalance as much as possible. balancing should therefore be systematically incorporated into the work process. top what causes unbalances in tooling operations? x: greater precision measuring and testing equipment is just as important as the accompanying software to ensure that tools perform exactly as planned, they must themselves be manufactured with precision. with our universal measuring machines, tools can be measured to the micrometer and checked to ensure they correspond to the requirements. top measurements in the coordinate measuring system the measured probe points are assigned by the measuring machines to a specific length measurement system along a specific axis of travel. the measuring software then processes this information and assigns it to specific points within the entire coordinate measuring system. based on the coordinates determined in this way, the cmm software then calculates the values for quantities that are not measured directly—such as lengths, angles, distances between two measuring points, and so on. the measuring points (actual values) determined in the coordinate measuring system (cms) are finally compared with the values that result from the specifications—such as the tool designs (nominal values). if these do not correspond—that is, if there are measurement deviations, whether due to manufacturing defects or wear and tear—appropriate corrective action can then be taken. what are 3d measuring machines ? the term “3d measuring machines” is generally used to designate measuring machines that can measure the three-dimensional dimensions of a measurement object in a relatively short time—ideally in real time. when applying compact linear or matrix-array cameras, some of these inspection machines can even be handheld or at least portable. however, portable cmms are generally slightly less accurate than conventional inspection machines. center coordinate measurement technology many measuring machines use what is known as coordinate measuring technology. the measuring machine (the full designation is “coordinate measuring machine,” cmm) uses a suitable sensor to enter the exact coordinates of specific points on the surface of the workpiece. in most cases, the coordinate system is created parallel to the orthogonal travel axes of the coordinate measuring systems. non-contact probing non-contact probing, on the other hand, uses cameras, laser triangulation sensors, and other methods, such as optical or electrical sensors. the measuring process takes place here without a measuring sensor ever coming into contact with the workpiece. under certain circumstances, this can significantly speed up the

»titanium« overview applications software & integration options & accessories technical specifications faq info pool 33-66 faq frequently asked questions top what are the main functions of the »titan« measuring machine? the »titan« enables high-precision measurement and inspection of a wide variety of cutting tools and workpieces. it combines state-of-the-art sensor technology and optical systems for exact measurement. top what is the measuring accuracy of the »titan«? the »titan«'s« measuring accuracy lies in the micrometer range, enabling extremely precise results: e xy = 2.0 μm + (l/250 mm) μm and e x = 1.3 μm + (l/300 mm) μm. top what types of tools can be measured using the »titan«? the »titan« can measure a wide variety of tools, such as milling cutters, drill bits, threading tools, gear-cutting tools, and many more. top what software is used for control and evaluation? the device is operated by the powerful zoller »pilot 4.0« software, which offers intuitive operation and comprehensive evaluation capabilities. additionally, there are additional software options tailored to each specific application. top how many cnc-controlled axes does the device have? the »titan« features 6 cnc-controlled axes, which enable flexible and precise positioning of the workpiece. a 7th axis is available as an optional addition. top what sensors and cameras are built into the »titan«? the »titan« is equipped with two high-definition cameras and a sensor for measuring the preparation of the cutting edges, ensuring exact measurements. top how simple is the »titan« operation for users? thanks to its user-friendly software (including the zoller measuring program assistant »«elephant»«) and ergonomic design, the operation of »the« »titan« is very simple and intuitive. top what are the benefits of automatic level control? automatic level adjustment ensures that the measuring machine is always optimally aligned, which improves measuring accuracy. top how is the quality of the measurement results ensured? the quality of the measurement results is ensured through regular calibration, high-quality components, and precise software. zoller is an accredited calibration laboratory in accordance with din en iso/iec 17025:2018. top what optional accessories are available for the »titan«? various accessories are available for the »titan«, including additional clamping systems, software modules, and specific measurement adapters. top inspection & measuring: your advantages inspection & me

overview faq info pool 33-66 faq frequently asked questions top what is webtms? zoller-webtms tms tool management solutions is the web version of the tms desktop application, which can be used on various devices. since zoller-webtms was developed from the ground up, not all modules and functions of the tms desktop version are currently available. advantages of a web application: no installation is required on devices. any device with a browser (pc, smartphone, tablet, laptop, etc.) can access webtms immediately. installation, configuration, and maintenance are performed only on the host device, which significantly reduces administrative overhead. top what is webtms startup edition? the webtms startup edition is the first version of webtms to be released. it comes pre-installed on all presetting and measuring machines as well as tms hardware products (»keeper«, »autolock«, »toolorganizer«, »ztower«, »toolstation«, »cockpit«), so customers can get started immediately. as soon as the device has a network connection, simply start webtms. from that point on, the software can be used on any device with a browser without any additional installation. top can tms customers also use the webtms startup edition? this version of webtms is not compatible with tms because it is hosted on the ipc of the presetting and measuring machine or on a tms hardware product that is not designed for this dual use. using both systems simultaneously can lead to performance issues and crashes. a compatible on-premises version (in beta) that is installed and hosted on the customer’s server is currently under development. top how do i install or set up webtms? no installation is required, as webtms is already preinstalled on the presetting and measuring machine or a tms hardware product. you only need to create a trial license (or select a purchased license) and start webtms on the device that should serve as the host. optionally, you can configure the database, graphic, and document path. to allow access from other devices, the presetting and measuring machine or a tms hardware product must be connected to the network. access is via the standard ports 80 and 443. top how can a customer purchase or extend a license? currently, customers can contact their zoller representative to request a customized quote. the license is sent manually by the software deployment team, but this process will be automated in the future. going forward, customers will be able to use myzoller for this purpose.

x: why optimize setup time? these days, almost no machine or system manufactures just one product—they are typically reconfigured to produce different products as needed. this results in setup times during which the machine generally does not produce anything. top what does “setup time” mean? setup time is the period during which a machine or system is switched from manufacturing one product to another. for example, when manufacturing discrete parts, setup time is defined as the time from the last part of the old batch to the first part of the new batch. setup time is therefore not “waste” in the strict sense; however, since it involves, at least in part, machine downtime, longer setup times naturally reduce the productivity and efficiency of your production facilities. center 33-66 how do i optimize setup time? optimizing setup time means, above all, minimizing setup time! there are various approaches to achieving this goal. top analyze setup operations any process aimed at reducing setup time must always begin with an analysis of the setup operations: what steps are necessary? which steps are currently being taken, and how much time do they require? in what order are the steps carried out, and can this order be changed? which steps are truly necessary, and which ones can be optimized? top optimize batch sizes a thorough analysis must also address the following question: is it possible to reduce the overall frequency of systems that are retooled—that is, to reduce the number of product changeovers? less frequent retooling operations are, of course, less time-consuming and thus save money. at the same time, the costs saved as a result must be carefully weighed against the desire to keep inventory as low as possible—that is, to avoid overproduction of goods. and, of course, equipment utilization should remain as high as possible throughout this process. top external setup in the context of setup time, a distinction is made between external setup (activities that are possible while the production line is running) and internal setup (for which the system must be shut down). naturally, it is in your best interest to keep internal setup—which results in productivity losses—as short as possible. top digitization and automation with modern machinery, the thorough digitization and automation of setup processes is a crucial step. tool presetters, for example, can determine the necessary tool data for a cnc machine tool in advance—that is, measure the tools and apply t

d: Quick Tool Change with a Shrink Tool With a good heat-shrink tool, you can change tools quickly, simply, and reliably using various tool holders. Here, we’ll explain in more detail
x: quick tool change with a shrink tool with a good heat-shrink tool, you can change tools quickly, simply, and reliably using various tool holders. here, we’ll explain in more detail how this works and what benefits it offers. top what happens during tool shrink fitting? shrinking a tool does not mean that the size of the tool itself is reduced. instead, the tool holder—into which, for example, a drill or cutting tool is inserted—is heated briefly, precisely, and consistently so that it expands. this creates enough space in the tool holder to use the tool. as it cools, the material of the holder contracts consistently on all sides. this ensures that the tool is clamped with high rigidity, maximum clamping force, and proper centering. top why are specialized shrink fit holders needed? specialized tool holders—known as shrink fit holders—are usually used for shrinking. they are specifically designed to retain their shape despite repeated heating and cooling cycles. for example, they contain no moving parts, ensuring that their balance grade is maintained; it is also important that the concentricity of the shrink fit holder is very high, because otherwise even a very precisely centered tool will be of no use. compared to conventional chucks, shrink fit holders have the minor disadvantage that a separate chuck with the appropriate diameter is required for each shaft diameter. however, this is offset by the significantly higher concentricity, which is of great importance for high-quality machined workpieces. top what is a shrink-fit machine, and how does it work? a shrink-fit machine heats the shrink fit holder—the tool holder—consistently and quickly using inductive current (i.e., via a magnetic field). with the appropriate supplies and measuring devices, it not only ensures that the new tool is precisely centered when it is used, but it can also ensure the proper length accuracy and measure—and, if necessary, correct—this before the check of the shrink fit holder. appropriate sensors also prevent the shrink fit holder or the tool from overheating. automated tool heat shrink technology ensures, for example, that the overhang length and all other parameters important for machining the workpieces are automatically measured and correctly set—while still making the tool available again in the shortest possible time. this results in short setup times and low overall costs. high-quality shrink-fit devices also feature their own cooling unit, in which the shrink fit ho

from a purely linguistic perspective, the term “tool life” for cutting tools seems a bit counterintuitive. this is because it does not describe the time during which a tool sits idle and unused, but rather the exact opposite: tool life refers to the total time during which a cutting tool is in use (i.e., actually performing material removal) before it needs to be exchanged. time required to exchange the workpiece is therefore not included in the tool life. exchanging a tool, in turn, incurs costs in several ways: a new tool must be purchased and used, while the old one must be regrounded or disposed of. it takes labor time to remove the old tool (and, if necessary, regrind it later) as well as to use a new one. while the tool is being exchanged, the machine is idle and the production process comes to a standstill—so the more frequently an exchange is required, the greater the production downtime. you face higher storage and procurement costs for your tool inventory. longer tool life therefore results in less machine downtime and thus enables more effective overall operations, thereby reducing your production costs. purchasing new tools can be avoided by regrinding existing ones. regrinding the tool cutting edges significantly extends the lifetime of the cutting tool, thereby saving on the cost of purchasing new tools. the »edgecontrol« measuring machine is helpful here. the device detects the greatest amount of wear and tear on a cutting edge. this allows the tool to be reground only to the extent that is actually necessary, with µm-level accuracy. learn more about wear marks and defects along the cutting edge top 50-50 what factors affect tool life?
